latin.577: §. XVII. Sicuti verò SECULO XII, ita non minus XIII, & seqq. famosissimi Waldenses tàm vitàm, quàm doctrinam papalem, maximè de Transsubstantiatione, Innocentii III. auctoritate stabilitam, constanter & fortiter improbarunt, ut hoc nomine non præcipuum duntaxat locum inter veritatis Christianæ testes teneant, sed & primi Ecclesiæ Romanæ Reformatores dici mereantur.
latin.578: Quanquam hanc ipsam ob causam, quòd generoso pectore sese Papatui opposuerunt, Curia Romana omnibus artibus viribusque eos in exterminium persecuta sit. Persecutionum genera crudelissima, Waldensibus, sub nominibus Bulgarorum & Albigensium, illata, ex multis hujus Seculi Historicis, prolixissimè enarrat doctissimus Armachanus, libro dicto cap. postremo, seu 10, à §. 18. & 27. ad finem usque capitis; in compendium omnia redegit, Confessionem eorum de S. Cœna subnectens summariam, Philippus Morneus,
latin.579: postquam Innocentianum de Transsubstantiatione Decretum hisce præmisisset: Annotandum, inquit, Anno 1215, Innocentius III. Pontifex, in Concilio Lateranensi, decretalem promulgat, cujus initium: Firmiter credimus &c. quæ & Conversionis Formam definit, & huic monstro nomen imponit hisce verbis: Idem ipse Sacerdos & Sacrificium Jesus Christus, cujus corpus & sanguis in Sacramento Altaris, sub speciebus panis & vini, veraciter continentur: Transsubstantiatis pane in corpus & vino in Sanguinem potestate divina. Lib. 4. de Sacram. Missæ supposititio cap. 8. pag. 1649. initio.
latin.580: At è contra (pergit Morneus) eâdem ætate in Delphinatu, Provincia Narbonensi, Occitana & Aquitana, Albigenses, & graviter hâc Pontificiâ doctrinâ offenduntur, & fortiter in eam insurgunt, secundum S. Scripturæ normam & antiquiorum Patrum usum, & credere, & docere, & vivere nihilominus rati. Pontifex itaque evertendorum quam convertendorum studiosior, Dominicum in speciem concionaturum mittit, at re vera, Leopoldum Ducem Austriæ & Simonem Comitem de Monteforti, cum ingentibus copiis vi oppressuros: pecuniam in Turcas collectam, Cruciatam vocabant, non sine sacrilegio interversam, in eos convertit; regiones porrò illas igne & ferrô vastat, nil aliud interim consecutus, quam ut totâ Europa sparsi, per Italiam, Germaniam, Bohemiam, Angliam, intima Galliæ, puriorem doctrinam, quam extinguere curabat, dispergerent.
latin.581: Tandem subjicit Mornæus: Waldensium Confessio fidem faciat, quam consulere Lector ne dedignetur, quandoquidem omnia ferè Transsubstantiatorum argumenta solidè satis, pro tempore, ibi refutantur. Summa est: In S. Cœna secundum Institutionem Christi celebrata, fidelem, verum Christi corpus & sanguinem accipere: Panis interim aut vini naturam aut substantiam minimè mutari, verba enim Christi nullam Conversionem inducere; Et, si Elementum desineret, Sacramentum non ampliùs fore.
latin.582: Nihilo magis dici Christum sub speciebus existere, neque in pane, neque ex pane, neque cum pane. Non ibi esse Christum in corpore, naturali mansione, existenter & corporaliter, sed SPIRITUALITER, potenter, benedictè, in veritate; Secundum quam mansionem non aberit, neque abiturus sit à suis, in quorum cordibus habitat. Eos proinde solos, non alios CHRISTUM in Sacramentis recipere, qui intrinsècùs ejus spiritu vivificati sunt. Cæterum, corpus & sanguinem Christi à Fidelibus percipi debere, non autem sacrificari, aut venerationis causa, attolli, aut circumferri, pag. 1650.

pass_a.577: §. XVII. But just as in the XIIth AGE, so no less in the XIIIth and following, the most famous Waldenses constantly and strongly disapproved both the papal life and the papal doctrine — especially concerning Transubstantiation established by the authority of Innocent III — so that on this account they not only hold a chief place among the witnesses of Christian truth but also deserve to be called the first Reformers of the Roman Church.
pass_a.578: Although for this very cause — that with generous breast they opposed themselves to the Papacy — the Roman Curia with all arts and forces persecuted them to extermination. The most cruel kinds of persecutions inflicted on the Waldenses under the names of Bulgars and Albigenses the most learned Armachanus narrates at greatest length from many Historians of this Age, in the said book’s last chapter, or 10, from §. 18 and 27 to the end of the chapter; Philip Morneus reduced all into a compendium, appending a summary Confession of theirs concerning the Sacred Supper,
pass_a.579: after he had first set down the Innocentian Decree on Transubstantiation in these words: It is to be noted, he says, in the Year 1215 Innocent III the Pontiff, in the Lateran Council, promulgates a decretal whose beginning is Firmiter credimus &c., which both defines the Form of Conversion and imposes a name on this monster in these words: The same Himself Priest and Sacrifice Jesus Christ, whose body and blood in the Sacrament of the Altar, under the species of bread and wine, are truly contained: the bread having been Transubstantiated into body and the wine into Blood by divine power (spurious Book 4 On the Sacraments of the Mass ch. 8 p. 1649 beginning).
pass_a.580: But on the contrary (Morneus continues) in the same age in Dauphiné, the Narbonese, Occitan and Aquitanian Province, the Albigenses are both gravely offended by this Pontifical doctrine and rise strongly against it, nonetheless resolved to believe and teach and live according to the norm of Holy Scripture and the use of the more ancient Fathers. The Pontiff therefore more eager to overthrow than to convert sends Dominic in appearance to preach, but in truth Leopold Duke of Austria and Simon Count of Montfort with huge forces to oppress by violence: the money collected against the Turks — they called it the Crusade — turned without sacrilege against them; further he lays those regions waste with fire and iron, meanwhile achieving nothing else than that, scattered through all Europe — through Italy, Germany, Bohemia, England, the inmost parts of Gaul — they disperse the purer doctrine he was busy extinguishing.
pass_a.581: At last Morneus subjoins: Let the Waldenses’ Confession make faith, which let the Reader not disdain to consult, since nearly all the Transubstantiators’ arguments are there refuted solidly enough for the time. The Sum is: In the Sacred Supper celebrated according to Christ’s Institution, the faithful receives the true body and blood of Christ: Meanwhile the nature or substance of bread or wine is by no means changed, for Christ’s words induce no Conversion; And if the Element should cease, there would no longer be a Sacrament.
pass_a.582: Nor any more is Christ said to exist under the species, neither in the bread, nor from the bread, nor with the bread. Christ is not there in the body, by natural abiding, existently and corporally, but SPIRITUALLY, powerfully, blessedly, in truth; According to which abiding He will not be absent, nor about to depart from His own, in whose hearts He dwells. Those alone therefore, not others, receive CHRIST in the Sacraments who are inwardly vivified by His spirit. For the rest, the body and blood of Christ ought to be perceived by the Faithful, but not sacrificed, or lifted up for the sake of veneration, or carried about (p. 1650).

577: §.XVII: in Ages XII and XIII and after, the famous Waldenses steadily rejected papal life and doctrine — above all Transubstantiation fixed by Innocent III.
For that they hold a chief place among Christian-truth witnesses and deserve to be called the Roman Church’s first Reformers.
578: Because they opposed the Papacy with generous courage, the Roman Curia hunted them to extermination with every art and force.
Armachanus narrates the cruellest persecutions under the names Bulgars and Albigenses; Morneus digests it and appends their summary Confession on the Sacred Supper.
579: Morneus first notes Innocent III’s Lateran decretal of 1215: Firmiter credimus…
It defines Conversion’s form and names the monster: Christ’s body and blood truly contained under bread and wine species — bread Transsubstantiated into body, wine into Blood by divine power.
580: Same age: Albigenses in Dauphiné, Narbonne, Occitania, Aquitaine are offended and rise against the pontifical doctrine by Scripture and the older Fathers’ use.
Innocent, keener to overthrow than convert, sends Dominic for show but Montfort and Leopold with armies — crusade money turned on them; fire and iron only scatter the purer doctrine across Europe.
581: Morneus: consult the Waldensian Confession — it solidly answers most Transubstantiators’ arguments for its time.

Sum: in the Supper per Christ’s Institution the faithful receives Christ’s true body and blood; bread and wine nature/substance are not changed — His words induce no Conversion; if the element ceased, there would be no Sacrament.
582: Christ is not said to exist under the species — not in, from, or with the bread — not there corporally by natural abiding, but SPIRITUALLY, powerfully, blessedly, in truth, dwelling in His people’s hearts.

Only those inwardly vivified by His Spirit receive Christ in the Sacraments; body and blood are to be perceived by the Faithful — not sacrificed, elevated for veneration, or carried about. Stop before §.XVIII.
